steps.body:
How fast does a function change **on average** between two inputs? The **average rate of change** on [a, b] is

**(f(b) − f(a)) / (b − a)**

— total change in output, divided by total change in input. It is one number summarizing the whole interval.
Build the interval and read its rate.

widget.prompt: On y = x², slide B until the gap from A is exactly 2 — the interval from x = 1 to x = 3. Read the average rate off the line.
widget.successFeedback: Rise 8 over run 2 = 4. The average rate of change IS the slope of the secant line: it is what a straight road from A to B would have felt like, whatever the curve did in between.
widget.lowFeedback: The gap is under 2, so B has not reached x = 3 yet. Push it out.
widget.highFeedback: The gap has passed 2, so B is beyond x = 3. Pull it back.

predict.prompt: You'll build the secant from A at x = 1 out to B at x = 3 on y = x². Compared with the tangent slope AT A (2), the secant's slope will be…
predict.reveal: The secant's slope is (f(3) − f(1))/2 = 4, against 2 for the tangent at A. On a curve whose slope keeps growing, the stretch out to B crosses steeper ground than A itself — so the average beats the value at the start.

cml.actionGoal: Shrink the interval between two points and compare secant slope with the limiting tangent slope.

steps.body: Now divide by the input change.
explanationVariants: Outputs climb 8 while inputs climb 2, so on average the function rises 4 per unit of x.

widget.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x² on [1, 3]?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is only the top of the fraction — the output change. Divide by the input change 3 − 1 = 2 to get the RATE.
Don't divide by b = 3; divide by the input CHANGE b − a = 2. 8/2 = 4.

steps.body: The denominator is **b − a**, the input change — not b itself. And a **linear** function is the special case where the answer never depends on the interval: its average rate of change is always its slope.

explanationVariants: A line changes at the same rate everywhere, so any interval returns its slope: 3.

widget.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = 3x + 1 on [0, 10]?

commonErrors.feedback: 30 is the output change f(10) − f(0). Divide by the input change 10 to get 3.
1 is the y-intercept, which sets where the line STARTS — the rate of change is the slope, 3.

explanationVariants: Outputs rise 21 across an input rise of 3; 21 ÷ 3 = 7 per unit.

widget.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x² on [2, 5]?

commonErrors.feedback: 21 is just f(5) − f(2). The rate divides that by the input change 5 − 2 = 3: 21/3 = 7.
You divided by b = 5. The denominator is the input CHANGE, b − a = 3, giving 7.

explanationVariants: From −1 up to 8 is a climb of 9 over 3 units of input: rate 3.
hints: Evaluate f at both endpoints first — one of the outputs is negative.
f(4) = 8, f(1) = −1. Subtracting a negative: 8 − (−1) = 9. Divide by 3.

widget.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x² − 2x on [1, 4]?

commonErrors.feedback: You used 8 − 1 = 7 on top, but f(1) = −1, not 1. Subtracting the negative gives 8 − (−1) = 9, so 9/3 = 3.
9 is the output change. Divide by the input change 4 − 1 = 3 to finish: 3.

steps.body: One number for a whole interval.
takeaways: Average rate of change = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).
Divide by the input CHANGE b − a, never by b.
A line's average rate of change is its slope on every interval.
steps.teaser: Next: this exact number is the slope of a line you can SEE — the secant.

concept.body: Two steps, always: (1) evaluate f at both endpoints; (2) divide output change by input change, (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).

explanationVariants: Output climbs 4 over an input climb of 2 — the rate is 2.

widget.prompt: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x² on [0, 2]?

commonErrors.feedback: 4 is the output change f(2) − f(0). Divide by the input change 2 − 0 to get the rate: 2.
You may have divided 2/2 using the input change on top. Outputs go on top: (4 − 0)/2 = 2.
